prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1210; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the policyholder's driver reporting a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection earlier today, with a report of a wrist injury to the claimant.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage happened before coverage began.

Entry 3: Claimant is not represented by an attorney. Statement taken and recorded; the claimant described stopping behind a vehicle that did not move in time to avoid contact.

Entry 4: Reviewed photos submitted by the claimant. They confirm the rear bumper and tail lamp damage on the claimant's vehicle and the front-end damage on the other vehicle, which line up well with the described impact.

Entry 5: Medical records show a wrist fracture consistent in kind and force with the crash as described. No prior injury to the same body area is known from the claimant's history or available records.

Entry 6: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this type of fracture. Follow-up notes are being requested to confirm the reason for the extended course.

Entry 7: Claimant was contacted for a follow-up call. Added a few small details about the sequence of events, but the core account has stayed the same since the first report.

Entry 8: No independent witnesses have been identified. The only available accounts are the claimant's and the other driver's, plus the photos on file.

Entry 9: Some uncertainty remains about where the claimant was seated in the vehicle at impact. The claimant has not been able to clarify this in a way that resolves the question, so it will be noted in the file.

Entry 10: Vehicle damage has been reviewed against the described impact and matches it. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection records.

Entry 11: File is being referred for the next review step. Open items are the extended treatment records and the seating position question, and the claim remains under standard handling.
